extracted.intended_audience: US patent applicants, patent attorneys, patent agents, and inventors involved in US patent prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing an Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) with the USPTO, including what must be disclosed, who has the duty, timing, related-case cross-citing, and procedures for late or post-issue submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose known prior art (duty of candor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent applicant has a duty to disclose to the USPTO all known prior art or other information that may be material to the patentability of the invention in a pending application. To satisfy this duty of candor, the prior art information must be submitted to the USPTO in the form of an Information Disclosure Statement ("IDS").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites MPEP 2001 and 37 CFR 1.56. Simply inserting prior art information in the specification of a patent application will not suffice; an IDS must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who bears the duty to disclose
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty to disclose known and relevant prior art applies to all persons involved with the substantive preparation of the patent application: the applicant/client, the patent attorneys and patent agents handling the application, and each inventor named in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an ongoing obligation for the applicant and its patent practitioners during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: No obligation to search for prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no duty to search for prior art; the duty of candor requires disclosure only of known prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should weigh pros and cons of conducting a patentability search. If a search is performed and uncovers references, those references will need to be disclosed when applying for a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality standard — what is 'material to patentability'
rubrics_metrics.description: Material information is information that is 'material to the patentability' of the invention claimed — think of 'material' as something that calls into question the novelty of the claimed invention or might render it obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References MPEP and 37 CFR 1.56(b); includes anything a reasonable examiner would be substantially likely to consider important in deciding whether to allow an application. Case law example: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, Inc. (article not prior art found material to enablement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of information to include in an IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Include patents, published patent applications, Office Actions (particularly Office Actions in related US and foreign patent applications), and non-patent literature (NPL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any foreign Office Actions or foreign patent references should be accompanied by an English summary of the pertinent information. The IDS should also encompass other 'information' listed under 37 CFR 1.56, e.g., information on enablement, possible prior public uses, sales, offers to sell, derived knowledge, prior invention by another, inventorship conflicts, litigation statements, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-publication information and other non‑patent matters
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.56's definition of 'information' is broad and includes non-publication information such as enablement issues, possible prior public uses, sales, offers to sell, derived knowledge, prior invention by another, inventorship conflicts, and litigation statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality is not limited to prior art but embraces any information a reasonable examiner would consider important in deciding whether to allow an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum public accessibility requirement for NPL
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-patent literature or information must meet a minimum level of public accessibility to qualify as prior art (see MPEP § 2128.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If copies of NPL documents cannot be obtained, the information might not be publicly accessible; if copies are available, there is no excuse for failing to procure and include them in an IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-citing prior art across related applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine at filing whether a new US application is related to previously filed foreign or US applications; if related, cross-reference for purposes of filing IDSs in the group of related cases (cross-citing prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant regulations: 37 CFR 1.57(b) and MPEP 2001.05. Relatedness is often indicated by a priority claim to the same foreign application; in the absence of priority claims, relatedness can be shown by common inventors/assignee or similar subject matter (MPEP 2001.06(b)). Cross-citing ensures prior art uncovered in one case is considered in related cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing an IDS (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: File the IDS as soon as relevant prior art information is known; for new applications, file with the initial submission or shortly thereafter, preferably before the issuance of a first Office Action to avoid USPTO fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty of candor is ongoing; supplemental IDSs must be filed as new prior art is discovered. Multiple related pending applications may require multiple IDS filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing & procedures when new prior art is found after a Final Office Action or Notice of Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If new prior art is discovered after receiving a Notice of Allowance or Final Office Action: if the references were first discovered less than 3 months ago, the applicant may file the IDS and pay a USPTO IDS fee; if more than three months have passed since discovery, the applicant must file a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) and pay RCE fees to file a supplemental IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timing rule affects whether an IDS alone suffices or whether reopening prosecution via RCE is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for IDS after issue fee payment — QPIDS program
rubrics_metrics.description: After payment of the issue fee, the USPTO's Quick Path Information Disclosure Statement (QPIDS) program allows a streamlined request for consideration of an IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QPIDS requires certification, a petition to withdraw from issue after payment of the issue fee, and the Request for Continued Examination treated as a conditional RCE. The RCE fee will be refunded if no item of information in the IDS necessitates reopening prosecution. QPIDS certification and request are filed as a Web-based ePetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of undated prior art references in an IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Undated prior art references will generally not be considered by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential solutions: check archive.org for an archived earliest publication date; or if the applicant is certain the reference predates the application's priority date, submit a statement with the IDS indicating that the reference was known to the applicant prior to the priority date so the examiner may consider it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to disclose material information
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to disclose material information to the USPTO during prosecution may lead to a finding of inequitable conduct which may render a patent unenforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, the author recommends erring on the side of disclosing more rather than less to avoid attacks on an issued patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS form and submission requirement (cannot rely on specification alone)
rubrics_metrics.description: To satisfy the duty of candor, prior art information must be submitted in the form of an IDS rather than merely being inserted into the application specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IDS is the proper procedural mechanism; simply placing references in the specification does not meet the disclosure requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign references and language requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign Office Actions or foreign patent references submitted in an IDS should be accompanied by an English summary of the pertinent information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing English summaries aids examiner consideration and compliance with IDS content expectations.
